name: Komodo Airport
before:
The airport at Labuan Bajo sits on the western tip of Flores Island, in the East Nusa Tenggara province, and it exists largely because of what lies offshore. Komodo National Park is the draw, and this is the way in for almost everyone who goes. The name is a nod to the dragon itself, the monitor lizard found nowhere else, though most visitors arrive with boat trips, snorkelling and island hopping in mind as much as reptiles.

It was once called Mutiara II, and the shift to international status reflects how quickly Labuan Bajo has grown as a destination. Flights come in from Jakarta, Surabaya and Denpasar on Bali, which is the usual hop for anyone already on a two centre trip. There are also international services from Kuala Lumpur and Singapore, useful for clients who want to skip Bali altogether. Smaller regional flights connect onward across Flores to Bajawa, Ende and Maumere, which suits travellers heading east overland.

Labuan Bajo itself is the capital of West Manggarai Regency, a working harbour town that has taken on a second life as a base for boat charters and dive operators.
after:
The airport at Labuan Bajo sits on the island of Flores, in East Nusa Tenggara province. Komodo National Park is the draw, and the airport is the main way in. The name is a nod to the dragon itself, the giant lizard found in the wild nowhere else.

It was once called Mutiara II and became an international airport in 2024. Flights come in from Jakarta, Surabaya and Denpasar on Bali, the easy hop on a two centre trip. There are also international flights from Kuala Lumpur and Singapore, useful for clients who want to skip Bali altogether. Smaller regional flights head east to Bajawa, Ende and Maumere.

Labuan Bajo itself is the capital of West Manggarai Regency.

claims.claim: volcanic ash closure in November 2024
claims.why: Held back: ash from Mount Lewotobi Laki-laki, in East Flores, closed the airport from 9 November 2024 (detik; Wikipedia), with flights normal again from 17 November by detik's account, while Wikipedia gives the closure as 9 to 19 November. The FCDO's general Indonesia advice says ash clouds can affect flight schedules and regional airports. It replaces nothing in the old text; a line such as 'volcanic ash on Flores can close the airport, as it did for over a week in November 2024' would need Andy's say-so.

quote: Selasa, 19 Nov 2024 18:35 WIB

Mulai Minggu (17/11/2024) hingga hari ini, aktivitas penerbangan sudah normal kembali.

The old text names no operator, so nothing changes in the text.
